title: Ephemeral SLO smoother and atomic circuit latch (hotfix)
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Context: Production alerted on a cascade of tenant-level SLO violations in eu-west-1 during a short latency surge (2026-02-14). Root cause analysis showed two contributing issues: noisy instant SLO bookkeeping that caused frequent tenant promotion/demotion thrash and a race in the circuit state machine that allowed some circuits to flip-open and never transition back cleanly. This PR introduces a conservative, short-window SLO signal smoother (ephemeral-slo-smoother) plus an atomic latch for circuit transitions to prevent reopen flapping. Both changes are guarded behind feature flags and a default-safe config to allow immediate rollback. Motivation: reduce false-positive SLO enforcement actions during transient spikes, avoid unnecessary regional failover churn, and prevent circuits from ending up in a stuck-open state after concurrent transitions. Summary of changes: 1) New smoother: src/serving/slo/smoother.go implements an exponentially-weighted short-window smoother (default window 6s, decay alpha=0.5) for latency and error-rate signals used by the SLO enforcer. The smoother emits a sampled aggregated metric (slo_smoother_windowed_value) and an internal 'momentary_violation' token that the enforcer uses to decide short quarantines. 2) Atomic latch: src/serving/circuit/latch.go replaces the previous CAS-based soft transitions with a single-locked latch around reopen logic to guarantee a clear linearization point. This closes a race that could leave circuits open after simultaneous failure and manual intervention. 3) Ephemeral tenant quarantine: runtime/tenant/quarantine.go implements TTL-based transient quarantine (default TTL 30s, exponential backoff on repeat violations) that routes to a degraded slowpath rather than triggering immediate failover. 4) Regional failover guard: pkg/ops/region/failover.go adds an additional check that prevents regional failover for tenants currently in ephemeral quarantine unless the violation persists beyond the quarantine TTL. 5) Observability: added metrics slo_smoother_latency_exceeded_count, slo_smoother_active_windows, circuit_latch_state_transitions and tracing spans for smoother evaluation. 6) Tests and docs: unit tests under tests/serving/smoother_test.go and tests/serving/circuit_latch_test.go; runbook update in docs/runbooks/slo-smoother.md. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout across canary nodes in eu-west-1, monitor new metrics and error budgets for 48h, then enable cluster-wide. Hotfix rationale: given production impact and the minimal, well-scoped changeset, this landed as a hotfix with a short canary. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke in staging - [x] Feature flag gating added - [x] Runbook updated - [x] Metrics & alerts adjusted Detailed notes on safety and revert: both smoother and latch are togglable via runtime flags (runtime.slo.smoother.enabled, runtime.circuit.latch.enabled). Reverting is a config flip and rollback of the flag; no DB migrations involved. If immediate rollback required, flip flags and redeploy the routing config. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes. Performance: smoother is inexpensive (O(1) per sampled request) and latch uses a lock scoped only to the relevant circuit instance to avoid global contention. Related: addresses ENG-4132 (SLO thrash during latency microbursts), SRE-210 follow-up to incident 2026-02-14.
commits: Introduce ephemeral SLO smoother and basic unit tests
Add atomic circuit latch and transition tests
Implement TTL-based tenant quarantine and integrate with failover guard
Fix race in latch under heavy parallel reopen (test coverage)
